alignments.note: Relative pronoun with the *of* that English idiom requires after *beware*; no Greek preposition is expressed for it to answer to, so it is a rule 7 helper on the relative it fronts with. Head on *whom*.
Intensifying καί realized by *also*; rule 65's English-side test.
Imperative with the supplied periphrastic *do*, discontinuous under rule 15; head on the lexical verb.
Inflected verb with its supplied subject pronoun, discontinuous around *greatly* under rule 15; head on the lexical verb.
The first-person plural possessive adjective ἡμετέροις names the possessor itself and carries *our*, so the article realizes nothing; rule 54's ὁ καιρὸς ὁ ὑμέτερος.

review_notes: τοῖς ἡμετέροις λόγοις is decided by rule 54: the possessive adjective takes *our* and the article is unrepresented.

The fronted *of whom* keeps its *of* with the relative, no Greek preposition being expressed; giving *of* to φυλάσσου as a phrasal particle is the competing reading and is refused because the word governs the relative, not the verb.
